input: Audience: Wedding photographers with an established visual style who are refining ad messaging for couples deciding whether the photographer's approach will suit them. | Tension: A strong shorthand such as “no posing” can signal a candid style, but may also suggest the photographer will not help with portraits when couples want direction. | Argument: A wedding photographer's positioning is more useful when it distinguishes candid coverage from staged imagery without implying that couples will be left unguided when they want help. | Take: Describe the experience couples can expect across the day, including both candid coverage and requested portrait direction, rather than making an absolute claim that misstates the service. | Mechanism: The photographer reported that many couples value real moments and also ask for help with couple portraits. Messaging that reflects both parts can address the style preference without obscuring the practical support those couples may want. | Reader decision: Review prominent ad and landing-page claims for absolutes, then check whether they accurately describe both candid coverage and the guidance available for portraits.
